title: Augmentation-normalized single-site acyclic hypercover descent
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with its small pro-etale site in compatible universes [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention], and $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings. Let $W$ be a site object and $U_\bullet\to W$ an augmented simplicial object [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object]. Assume its finite proper-face matching objects exist, its degree-zero matching object is $W$, and each matching arrow is a covering [def-sfb-proper-face-matching-arrow]. Assume every $U_p$ is weakly contractible: evaluation there carries epimorphisms of set sheaves to surjections [sk-def-pe-weak-contractible]. For an integer-indexed strictly bounded-below complex $E$ of $R$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], write $T_U(E)^n=\bigoplus_{p+q=n,\,p\geq0}E^q(U_p)$ with differential $\delta+(-1)^p d_E$, $\delta=\sum_i(-1)^id_i^*$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-hypercover-total]. Let $\alpha_E:E(W)\to T_U(E)$ be restriction into bidegree $(0,q)$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-hypercover-augmentation]. All conclusions below are in abelian groups after forgetting scalars, with localization $Q$ into $D(\mathbf{Ab})$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

Evaluation of module sheaves at every $U_p$ is exact, without an affineness assumption, and carries every quasi-isomorphism of coefficient complexes to a quasi-isomorphism. For every quasi-isomorphism $f:E\to F$ between strictly bounded-below complexes, $T_U(f)$ is a quasi-isomorphism. For every strictly bounded-below termwise-injective complex $I$, $\alpha_I$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Thus for every bounded-below termwise-injective resolution $i:E\to I$, both $T_U(i)$ and $\alpha_I$ are quasi-isomorphisms.

Let $R\Gamma(W,-)$ be the actual right derived evaluation [def-sfb-right-derived-functor], and let $\rho_i:R\Gamma(W,QE)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q(I(W))$ be its canonical computation on $i$. Then
$$A_{U,E}=(Q T_U(i))^{-1}\,Q\alpha_I\,\rho_i:R\Gamma(W,QE)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q T_U(E)$$
is independent of $i$ and natural for all coefficient chain maps between strictly bounded-below complexes. Its normalization is $Q T_U(i) A_{U,E}=Q\alpha_I\rho_i$ for every such resolution. More explicitly, a coefficient homotopy $s:f\simeq g$ induces the total homotopy with component $(-1)^p s|_{U_p}$ on bidegree $(p,q)$, and a comparison $k:I\to I'$ with $ki\simeq i'$ satisfies $Q T_U(k)Q T_U(i)=Q T_U(i')$ and $Q\Gamma(W,k)\rho_i=\rho_{i'}$.

For any refinement $r:U'_\bullet\to U_\bullet$ over $W$, with $U'$ satisfying the same assumptions, restriction gives chain maps $r_E:T_U(E)\to T_{U'}(E)$ satisfying $r_I\alpha_I=\alpha'_I$, $r_I T_U(i)=T_{U'}(i)r_E$, and $Q r_E A_{U,E}=A_{U',E}$. These maps commute with coefficient maps and identity and composite refinements. For a sheaf $M$ in degree zero, $T_U(M[0])$ is the alternating section complex with degree $p$ term $M(U_p)$.

Injective objects and resolutions are as in [def-sp-injective-resolutions]; coefficient homotopies and K-injectivity are as in [def-pur-kinjective-complex].

source.place: Tag 09A2, label lemma-compute-cohomology; Tag 0946, sites-cohomology.tex label lemma-w-contractible. Agent refinement: signed homotopy, every-resolution normalization, coefficient naturality and refinement identities.

proof.text: For each $p$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-weakly-contractible-evaluation-exact] to $W=U_p$: its hypothesis is precisely the assumed surjectivity of evaluation on set-sheaf epimorphisms, in the coefficient universe. It gives preservation of homology by module evaluation. Applying this to a short exact sequence viewed as a three-term complex proves exactness, and $H^q(f(U_p))=H^q(f)(U_p)$ proves preservation of quasi-isomorphisms. Forgetting the $R(U_p)$-module structure does not change kernels, images, or these equalities. Nothing in this application requires $U_p$ to be affine.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-hypercover-total-quasi-iso] to the two bounded-below coefficient complexes and the coefficient quasi-isomorphism. Weak contractibility supplies its section-surjectivity hypothesis by the set-sheaf epi criterion. Its total is the published signed total. Forgetting module scalars preserves homology, so the same map is a quasi-isomorphism of abelian-group complexes.

source.place: Tag 09A2, lemma-compute-cohomology, second paragraph; finite-diagonal comparison

proof.text: A covering map induces an epimorphism of represented sheaves: two maps out of its codomain agreeing after pullback agree by sheaf separation on the generated covering sieve. Apply this to every matching arrow in the slice. In degree zero the terminal matching object is canonically isomorphic to the identity over W; in degree one retain the product fan; in higher degrees transport the matching arrow across the recorded limiting-cone isomorphism. These are exactly the hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-hypercover-injective-row], giving the actual augmented section-row quasi-isomorphism for every injective module sheaf.

source.place: Tags 01GE, lemma-acyclic-hypercover-sheaves, and 01GW, lemma-injective-trivial-cech, ringed-module analogue; Tag 00WN

proof.text: Now let $I$ be strictly bounded below with injective terms. Step 3 supplies the row hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-hypercover-injective-complex-comparison], which therefore makes the actual restriction augmentation $\alpha_I:I(W)\to T_U(I)$ a quasi-isomorphism. This is the map into the $(0,q)$ summands, since [def-weil-pbc-proetale-hypercover-augmentation] specifies precisely that augmentation. Together with step 2 this proves both quasi-isomorphism assertions for every $i:E\to I$.

For a coefficient homotopy $s:f\simeq g$, put $H^{p,q}=(-1)^p s^q(U_p)$, landing in bidegree $(p,q-1)$. Naturality of the sheaf morphisms $s^q$ gives $\delta s=s\delta$. With $D=\delta+(-1)^p d$, the horizontal terms in $DH+HD$ are $(-1)^p\delta s+(-1)^{p+1}s\delta=0$, and the vertical terms are $ds+sd=f-g$. Hence $DH+HD=T_U(f)-T_U(g)$. There is no convergence issue: $H$ acts one summand at a time in each finite diagonal. Evaluation at $W$ likewise sends $s$ to a homotopy. By the homotopy-category localization in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], both functors therefore send homotopic maps to equal derived maps.

source.place: Tag 09A2, signed-total convention; agent calculation of coefficient homotopy

proof.text:
The pro-etale site of the statement is small in the chosen universe, so [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] shows that $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ is Grothendieck abelian and that every complex of $R$-module sheaves has a K-injective resolution; this is the hypothesis of [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] for the additive functor $\Gamma(W,-):\operatorname{Mod}(R)\to\mathbf{Ab}$, so $R\Gamma(W,-)$ and its unit exist. By [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives] $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ has enough injectives, so [lem-sc-bounded-below-injective-resolution-existence] gives every strictly bounded-below $E$ a bounded-below termwise-injective resolution $i:E\to I$; hence $A_{U,E}$ is defined for every such $E$. Mathlib CochainComplex.isKInjective_of_injective says directly that each bounded-below termwise-injective complex is K-injective. For two resolutions $i:E\to I$ and $i':E\to I'$, use [lem-sp-kinjective-comparison-principle] with $s=i$ and target $I'$ to obtain a chain map $k:I\to I'$ with $ki\simeq i'$. Step 5 gives $QT_U(k)QT_U(i)=QT_U(i')$. Writing $\eta$ for the actual right-derived evaluation unit of [def-sfb-right-derived-functor], its computation on $i$ is $\rho_i=\eta_I^{-1}R\Gamma(W,Qi)$. Unit naturality and $Qk\,Qi=Qi'$ give
$$Q\Gamma(W,k)\rho_i=\eta_{I'}^{-1}R\Gamma(W,Qk)R\Gamma(W,Qi)=\rho_{i'}.$$
This uses the unit of the specified derived functor, not an arbitrary isomorphism.

Set $a_i=QT_U(i)$ and $b_i=Q\alpha_I\rho_i$. Steps 2 and 4 make $a_i,b_i$ invertible. Define $A_i=a_i^{-1}b_i$, so $a_iA_i=b_i$. For the comparison $k$ of step 6, augmentation naturality gives $QT_U(k)b_i=b_{i'}$ and step 5 gives $QT_U(k)a_i=a_{i'}$. Consequently $a_{i'}A_i=b_{i'}$, and cancellation of the invertible $a_{i'}$ yields $A_i=A_{i'}$. This proves independence and the normalization for every resolution, not merely for a selected one.

source.place: Tag 070Y, lemma-K-injective-defined; agent cancellation using the actual augmentation

proof.text:
For a coefficient chain map $f:E\to F$, take resolutions $i:E\to I$, $j:F\to J$, which exist by step 6. The comparison principle with quasi-isomorphism $i$ and K-injective target $J$ supplies $k:I\to J$ with $ki\simeq jf$. The signed homotopy of step 5 gives $QT_U(k)QT_U(i)=QT_U(j)QT_U(f)$. The unit computation in step 6, with $Qk\,Qi=Qj\,Qf$, gives $Q\Gamma(W,k)\rho_i=\rho_j R\Gamma(W,Qf)$. Finally, augmentation naturality gives $QT_U(k)Q\alpha_I=Q\alpha_JQ\Gamma(W,k)$. Substitute these three equalities in step 7 and cancel $QT_U(j)$ to obtain
$$QT_U(f)A_{U,E}=A_{U,F}R\Gamma(W,Qf).$$
Thus naturality holds for every coefficient chain map, without requiring a strictly commuting resolution square.

source.place: Tags 070I and 070Y; agent naturality calculation for a homotopy-commuting resolution square

proof.text:
For a refinement $r$, define $r_E$ on the $(p,q)$ summand by $E^q(U_p)\to E^q(U'_p)$. Commutation of $r$ with faces makes it commute with $\delta$, and restrictions commute with $d_E$, so it is a chain map. Restriction functoriality gives $r_I\alpha_I=\alpha'_I$ and $r_IT_U(i)=T_{U'}(i)r_E$. After applying $Q$ and composing with $A_{U,E}$, these identities and step 7 give
$$QT_{U'}(i)\,Qr_E A_{U,E}=Qr_I Q\alpha_I\rho_i=Q\alpha'_I\rho_i=QT_{U'}(i)A_{U',E}.$$
Cancel $QT_{U'}(i)$, invertible by step 2 for $U'$, to obtain the desired refinement normalization. On each summand coefficient maps commute with restriction, the identity refinement restricts by the identity, and restriction for a composite is the composite restriction; hence all these identities hold already as chain maps. For $E=M[0]$, only $q=0$ survives, so degree $p$ is $M(U_p)$ and the total differential is precisely $\sum_j(-1)^j d_j^*$. In Lean the row restrictions are the maps of the actual opposite-simplicial restriction functor; its map_id and map_comp laws give the row identities, which termwise extension and totalization preserve.
